orientation_entry.title: Python & pandas warm-up
orientation_entry.description: A short bridge from spreadsheet thinking to readable Python. Milestone 1 introduces the path; the two complete orientation lessons arrive in Milestone 2.

objectives.F1: Distinguish reporting, fixed rules, and supervised machine learning.

lessons.title: Reporting, rules, or machine learning?
lessons.scenario: A BPO operations lead brings six requests to the analytics team. Some need a dashboard, some need a fixed business rule, and some ask for a prediction from historical examples.

understand.title: Reporting describes what is known
understand.body: A report summarizes recorded events: yesterday's volume, average handle time by queue, or current backlog. Excel PivotTables and Power BI visuals are excellent for these questions. A report may reveal a pattern, but it does not by itself learn how to predict a future outcome.

understand.title: Rules apply decisions you already know
understand.body: A rule follows an explicit instruction such as ‘route Critical cases to Tier 2.’ Rules are transparent and dependable when the conditions are stable. They do not learn from examples; an analyst or policy owner writes the logic.

understand.title: Supervised ML learns from labeled examples
understand.body: Supervised machine learning connects past inputs to a known outcome, then estimates that outcome for a new case. ‘Which open cases are likely to miss SLA?’ is an ML-shaped question when historical cases contain both prediction-time features and the final SLA result. ML is useful only when the prediction changes a real decision.

activity.title: Choose the simplest suitable tool
activity.instructions: Classify each request by the kind of answer it needs. Use ML only when the request asks for an unknown outcome learned from examples.

scenarios.prompt: How many voice contacts arrived yesterday?
scenarios.rationale: The contacts have already happened, so this is a summary of known records.

scenarios.prompt: Route every Critical-priority case to Tier 2.
scenarios.rationale: The condition and action are explicitly known.

scenarios.prompt: Which currently open cases are likely to miss SLA?
scenarios.rationale: The outcome is not known yet and can be learned from labeled historical cases.

scenarios.prompt: Show average handle time by queue last month.
Send an alert whenever backlog exceeds 500 cases.
scenarios.rationale: A fixed threshold completely defines the behavior.

scenarios.prompt: Estimate the probability of a repeat contact in the next seven days.
scenarios.rationale: This asks for an uncertain future outcome estimated from past examples.

lab.title: Label three analyst requests
lab.instructions: Edit only the three quoted values. Use reporting, rules, or ml. Then run the checkpoint.

checkpoints.label: Yesterday's volume is reporting
checkpoints.pass_message: Known historical volume belongs in reporting.
checkpoints.fail_message: Yesterday's completed volume is a known fact, so use reporting.

checkpoints.label: Critical routing is a rule
checkpoints.pass_message: An explicit routing condition is a fixed rule.
checkpoints.fail_message: The priority condition and routing action are already known, so use rules.

checkpoints.label: Repeat-contact risk is ML
checkpoints.pass_message: An uncertain future outcome learned from examples is an ML task.
checkpoints.fail_message: Repeat-contact risk is an unknown future outcome, so use ml.

checks.prompt: A manager wants last week's CSAT by channel. What should you start with?

options.label: A report
options.rationale: Correct: the values are already known and only need summarizing.

options.label: A fixed rule
options.rationale: A rule performs an action; it does not summarize recorded scores.

options.label: A machine-learning model
options.rationale: A model is unnecessary because no unknown outcome is being predicted.

checks.prompt: Which request is best shaped for supervised ML?

options.label: List all queues
options.rationale: This is a straightforward lookup or report.

options.label: Predict whether a new case will be reopened
options.rationale: Correct: it asks for an unknown labeled outcome for a new case.

options.label: Escalate every P1 case
options.rationale: This is a complete fixed rule.

checks.prompt: Why should an analyst prefer a rule when the decision logic is already complete and stable?

options.label: Rules always have higher accuracy
options.rationale: Rules do not have predictive accuracy unless they are being evaluated as predictions.

options.label: Rules are transparent and do not need learned examples
options.rationale: Correct: explicit stable logic is simpler to explain and maintain.

options.label: ML cannot use tabular data
options.rationale: Supervised ML commonly uses tabular data.

lessons.takeaway: Use the simplest tool that answers the question: reports for known facts, rules for known decisions, and supervised ML for unknown outcomes that can be learned from labeled examples.
